limitations: GAAP income-statement and non-GAAP reconciliation figures are quarterly USD thousands. The first 2025 three-month column is selected; adjacent columns are prior-year, prior-quarter percentage comparisons, or six-/nine-month cumulative values.

The issuer's non-GAAP common income adds merger, restructuring/severance, and signed tax adjustments to GAAP common income. The reduction in adjustments means the GAAP common-income increase is larger than the non-GAAP increase; neither measure is a substitute for the other.

Total and fee-based client assets are end-period USD-million stocks. These two SEC exhibits do not provide a selected numeric net-new-assets bridge, so the quarter-to-quarter asset change must not be labelled net inflow or attributed solely to market performance.

Global Wealth Management and Institutional Group are segment measures, not an exhaustive reconciliation to consolidated GAAP net income. The selected rows do not prove recurrence of investment-banking revenue or the absence of other segment/corporate effects.
Selected rows do not audit all financial advisors, client-flow components, loan credit quality, capital adequacy, or every footnote.

reviews.rationale: Selected SEC exhibit rows for the two calendar quarters show a sequentially stronger GAAP earnings picture: net revenues, pretax income, net income and net income available to common all rose, and the increase in pretax income exceeded the increase in total non-interest expenses, so the expense build did not offset the revenue build in the displayed rows. Both operating segments contributed, with the wealth segment showing higher revenues and pretax income alongside higher end-of-period total and fee-based client assets, and the institutional segment also improving on both displayed lines. The company-defined non-GAAP reconciliation shrank because merger-related and restructuring/severance adjustments were smaller, so non-GAAP net income available to common rose by less than GAAP net income available to common; the GAAP improvement is therefore not merely an artifact of shrinking adjustments, but the non-GAAP measure also embeds a smaller tax-related adjustment, so the two bases should not be read as interchangeable. The income tax provision rose in absolute terms alongside higher pretax income; that is a larger tax expense, not a reduced tax drag, and no effective-rate conclusion is drawn from these selected rows. Uncertainty is material: the extract is a set of selected displayed rows rather than complete filings, all comparisons are sequential displayed-value arithmetic rather than year-over-year, and no segment revenue mix, compensation ratio, client-asset flow decomposition, share count, capital return, credit or balance-sheet detail, or management guidance is present in the extract, so the drivers of the revenue and expense moves are unresolved and no causal attribution is asserted. The thesis is a source-bounded baseline with no valuation or conviction claim, so the appropriate research state is to maintain it at the existing conviction while recording the updated selected-source baseline; evidence that would change the view includes full-filing segment and flow detail, year-over-year comparables, guidance versus realized results, and any disclosure showing the sequential revenue gain was concentrated in volatile items or that expense growth was structural.
